patterns.name: Agent Platforms
patterns.tag: Governed agent lifecycle, PHI guardrails, HITL for clinical and claims

features.name: Agent Lifecycle Management
features.lookFor: Versioning, dev/test/prod promotion, approval gates, rollback, central agent catalog
features.why: Turns pilot sprawl into a governed portfolio

features.name: Model Choice & Portability
features.lookFor: Multi-provider models, per-agent selection, easy swaps, own-tenant/VPC deployment
features.why: Avoids model lock-in; protects cost and leverage

features.name: Enterprise & Healthcare Connectors
features.lookFor: Permission-aware connectors: Snowflake, SharePoint, CRM, ITSM, FHIR/EHR, claims
features.why: Governed data access cuts integration effort

features.name: Open Interoperability (MCP/A2A)
features.lookFor: Consume/expose MCP tools, A2A agent collaboration, OpenAPI/REST actions
features.why: Reusable tools; agents collaborate across platforms

features.name: Agent Identity & Least Privilege
features.lookFor: IdP-registered agents, OAuth on-behalf-of, scoped tool permissions, vaulted secrets
features.why: Prevents PHI over-exposure; makes access auditable

features.name: Guardrails & HIPAA/PHI Safety
features.lookFor: PHI redaction, prompt-injection defense, grounding checks, signed BAA, residency
features.why: Lets pilots pass privacy and compliance review

features.name: Human-in-the-Loop Controls
features.lookFor: Approval steps, confidence thresholds, escalation, per-agent autonomy levels
features.why: Safe automation; humans own consequential decisions

features.name: Evaluation & Quality Gates
features.lookFor: Eval datasets, LLM-as-judge, regression tests, red-teaming, CI/CD gates
features.why: Evidence-based scaling; supports model-risk governance

features.name: Observability & Audit Trail
features.lookFor: Step-level traces, tokens/cost/latency, OpenTelemetry export, immutable action logs
features.why: Debug failures; prove actions for HIPAA audit

features.name: FinOps & Domain Isolation
features.lookFor: Cost attribution by agent/domain, budgets, quotas, isolated domain workspaces
features.why: Keeps consumption costs sustainable; enables federated adoption

patterns.takeaway: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service (82.5%) is the best fit as the pro-code runtime, paired with Copilot Studio as the governed low-code front door under shared Entra Agent ID and Agent 365 governance. Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (80.0%) and AWS Bedrock AgentCore (77.5%, portability and guardrail leader) are close alternatives and exception paths; the small gap means cloud alignment should decide. Key risks are unconfirmed BAA scope for Foundry Agent Service and partner models, Azure runtime lock-in, and roadmap churn across all vendors.

patterns.name: Agent Frameworks
patterns.tag: Durable, model-agnostic orchestration for multi-step prior-auth and care workflows

features.name: Stateful Orchestration & Durability
features.lookFor: Graphs/state machines, checkpoints, resume-after-failure, long runs, deterministic replay
features.why: Multi-day healthcare workflows must survive restarts

features.name: Model-Agnostic Abstractions
features.lookFor: Multi-provider models, structured outputs, streaming; config-only model swaps
features.why: Protects code investment as models and pricing change

features.name: MCP / A2A Tool Protocols
features.lookFor: Consume MCP servers, expose agents via MCP/A2A, typed tools
features.why: Plugs into enterprise tools without bespoke glue

features.name: Multi-Agent Patterns
features.lookFor: Supervisor/worker, hand-off, hierarchical, parallel fan-out composition
features.why: Decomposes complex domains; reusable patterns cut defects

features.name: Memory & Context Management
features.lookFor: Short/long-term memory, pluggable stores, summarization, PHI-aware retention
features.why: Improves quality and cost; keeps state HIPAA-compliant

features.name: Human-in-the-Loop Interrupts
features.lookFor: Native interrupt/resume to pause for review, edits, continue
features.why: Enables graduated autonomy on consequential healthcare actions

features.name: Testing & Debuggability
features.lookFor: Test harnesses, model/tool mocks, eval hooks, visual debugging, reproducibility
features.why: Scales many agents safely; cuts rework after upgrades

features.name: OpenTelemetry-Native Tracing
features.lookFor: GenAI-convention OTel spans exportable to any backend
features.why: Portable, unified observability; no per-team monitoring silo

features.name: Deployment Portability & Security
features.lookFor: Containers/K8s/serverless anywhere; sandboxed execution; vaulted secrets; supply-chain hygiene
features.why: Runs near sensitive data; passes security review

features.name: Ecosystem Maturity & LTS
features.lookFor: Community, license, backing, release cadence, stable APIs, commercial support
features.why: Avoids costly rewrites from churn or abandonment

patterns.takeaway: LangGraph is the best fit (85.0%), leading on durable checkpointed state, native interrupt/resume for human approval, debug/eval tooling and a stable 1.x API, and should be the primary standard. CrewAI (65.0%) is a sanctioned exception for low-risk role-based automation, LlamaIndex is used as a document/retrieval component, and Microsoft Agent Framework replaces Semantic Kernel and AutoGen (neither should be chosen for new work) as the .NET path. Key risk: LangGraph tracing is LangSmith-first, so the standard must mandate OTel export and secure BAA or self-hosted LangSmith.
patterns.platformNote: Snowflake is the governed data and context layer rather than an agent framework: agents should reach PHI via Cortex Agents, Cortex Search and Cortex Analyst (as MCP tools or through langchain-snowflake), with checkpoints, traces and eval results landing in Snowflake.

patterns.name: MCP Ecosystems
patterns.tag: Governed tool access to EHR, FHIR, Snowflake with least privilege

features.name: Spec Compliance & Currency
features.lookFor: Current MCP spec, streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 auth, fast spec updates
features.why: Stale implementations break interoperability and security

features.name: Enterprise Registry & Discovery
features.lookFor: Private curated registry: owner, version, data class, scopes, lifecycle
features.why: Prevents shadow MCP; one inventory of PHI tools

features.name: Delegated Auth & Scopes
features.lookFor: IdP OAuth, on-behalf-of tokens, per-tool scopes, no static keys
features.why: Agent access matches user entitlements for PHI, audit

features.name: Central Gateway & Policy
features.lookFor: Gateway enforcing allow/deny lists, parameter validation, rate limits, DLP
features.why: One control point for all agent-to-tool traffic

features.name: MCP Threat Protection
features.lookFor: Defenses for tool poisoning, prompt injection, rug-pull, confused deputy
features.why: One compromised tool can exfiltrate PHI

features.name: Healthcare & Enterprise Servers
features.lookFor: Supported servers for Snowflake, FHIR/EHR, claims, ServiceNow, M365, CRM
features.why: Removes custom connector work; reveals build gaps

features.name: Hosting Flexibility
features.lookFor: Kubernetes, serverless, managed or on-prem hosting; controlled local servers
features.why: Portability, data residency, tools near on-prem EHR

features.name: Tool-Call Observability & Audit
features.lookFor: Per-call logs with PHI masking, OpenTelemetry export, tamper-evident retention
features.why: Chain of custody for HIPAA audits, investigations

features.name: Server Dev Lifecycle
features.lookFor: SDKs, templates, contract tests, CI/CD, versioning, OpenAPI-to-MCP wrapping
features.why: Turns existing APIs into governed tools repeatably

features.name: FinOps & Usage Analytics
features.lookFor: Per-tool/agent metering, quotas, downstream cost attribution, adoption dashboards
features.why: Controls hidden downstream costs; shows value by domain

patterns.takeaway: Best fit is a cloud MCP gateway ecosystem, with AWS Bedrock AgentCore (75.0%) and Microsoft (72.5%) effectively tied; pick the one matching the primary hyperscaler and identity estate. Custom MCP Servers are the build standard for FHIR/claims domain servers and GitHub MCP Server is a sanctioned SDLC server, but both must sit behind the gateway and private registry. Key risks are shadow MCP, PHI leakage through tool responses (APIM cannot inspect streaming bodies) and MCP-specific threats like tool poisoning.

patterns.name: RAG Frameworks
patterns.tag: Permission-aware, cited answers over medical policies, benefits, clinical content

features.name: Document Ingestion & Parsing
features.lookFor: Layout-aware parsing of PDFs, scans/OCR, tables, forms, C-CDA
features.why: Parsing quality caps retrieval quality

features.name: Chunking & Embedding Flexibility
features.lookFor: Semantic/hierarchical chunking, metadata enrichment, pluggable embedding models
features.why: Tune per content type; avoid embedding lock-in

features.name: Hybrid Retrieval & Re-Ranking
features.lookFor: BM25 plus vector, metadata filters, re-rankers, query rewriting
features.why: Exact codes and dates need keyword precision

features.name: Permission-Aware Retrieval
features.lookFor: Source ACL trimming, identity propagation, PHI-aware filters, permission sync
features.why: Never surface records users cannot see

features.name: Grounding & Citations
features.lookFor: Passage-level citations, faithfulness checks, confidence, safe refusal
features.why: Verifiable answers build clinician trust

features.name: RAG Evaluation
features.lookFor: Context precision/recall, faithfulness metrics, golden sets, A/B tests
features.why: Measured quality justifies scale-up, catches regressions

features.name: Freshness & Incremental Indexing
features.lookFor: Change-driven re-index, delete propagation, effective-dated versions, SLAs
features.why: Stale policy answers create compliance risk

features.name: Advanced / Agentic Retrieval
features.lookFor: Agentic multi-step, text-to-SQL, GraphRAG, multimodal retrieval
features.why: Questions span documents and structured data

features.name: Portability & Platform Proximity
features.lookFor: Model/store agnostic; in-platform retrieval like Snowflake Cortex Search
features.why: Keeps PHI governed and avoids lock-in

features.name: Cost & Performance Efficiency
features.lookFor: Embedding/index cost controls, caching, token efficiency, latency SLAs
features.why: Keeps enterprise-wide rollout economical

patterns.takeaway: LlamaIndex (70.0%) is the best-fit RAG framework standard thanks to its best-in-class parsing of table-heavy and scanned healthcare documents, with Snowflake Cortex Search recommended as the default governed retrieval index for PHI content. Haystack (alternative framework for sovereign/on-prem use) and Azure AI Search (exception path for SharePoint-centric, permission-critical corpora) tie at 67.5%, while LangChain/LangGraph serves as the agent-orchestration layer and Semantic Kernel should not be a new standard. Key risk: permission-aware retrieval is weak across most frameworks, and Azure AI Search copies PHI out of Snowflake and relies on Preview ACL features.

patterns.name: Vector Search
patterns.tag: Secure embedding search for RAG, semantic search and agent memory

features.name: Performance & Scale
features.lookFor: Proven ANN recall/latency at 100M–1B+ vectors, high QPS, scaling
features.why: Large indexes drive user experience and infrastructure cost

features.name: Hybrid Search & Filtering
features.lookFor: Vector plus BM25/sparse fusion; metadata filtering without recall collapse
features.why: Exact identifiers and filters make results accurate, compliant

features.name: Security & HIPAA Readiness
features.lookFor: RBAC, doc-level security, CMK encryption, private networking, audit, BAA
features.why: Embeddings and chunks can reveal PHI

features.name: Deployment Portability
features.lookFor: Managed SaaS, BYOC, self-hosted/on-prem, and in-platform vector options
features.why: Avoids lock-in; in-platform search removes separate systems

features.name: Multi-Tenancy & Isolation
features.lookFor: Per-tenant isolation, quotas, noisy-neighbor protection, per-tenant backup/restore
features.why: Enables federated domain adoption on a shared service

features.name: Index Types & Compression
features.lookFor: HNSW/IVF/DiskANN, quantization, tiered storage, sparse/multi-vector support
features.why: Compression and tiering cut memory cost at scale

features.name: Real-Time Updates & Deletes
features.lookFor: Low-latency upserts/deletes, consistency, streaming/CDC ingest, re-embedding
features.why: Freshness and right-to-delete need immediate, reliable deletes

features.name: Embedding & Ecosystem Integration
features.lookFor: Built-in embeddings, SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, MCP, Snowflake/Kafka integrations
features.why: Less glue code, faster delivery across domains

features.name: Reliability, HA/DR
features.lookFor: Replication, multi-AZ/region, backups/PITR, zero-downtime upgrades, SLAs, observability
features.why: Vector search becomes tier-1 clinical infrastructure

features.name: FinOps & Pricing
features.lookFor: Clear pricing, per-index/tenant cost attribution, scale-to-zero, forecasting
features.why: Supports chargeback and avoids budget surprises

patterns.takeaway: Qdrant (87.5%) is the best fit as the portable enterprise vector standard, with Elasticsearch (85.0%) as co-leader where hybrid lexical search and query-time document-level security matter most; the Tier 1 choice between them should be settled by PoC. Amazon OpenSearch and Azure AI Search remain sanctioned exceptions for AWS-native Bedrock and M365/SharePoint RAG, Weaviate fits heavily multi-tenant use but has limited HIPAA scope, and Pinecone carries the highest lock-in and corporate uncertainty. Snowflake Cortex Search should be the Tier 0 default for Snowflake-resident corpora; the key risks are PHI leakage without query-time trimming and lock-in, mitigated by keeping chunks and embeddings in Snowflake as the system of record.

patterns.name: Gateway, Observability
patterns.tag: AI control plane: model routing, cost control, tracing, HIPAA audit

features.name: Multi-Model Routing & Failover
features.lookFor: One API, policy-based routing, fallback, load balancing, version pinning
features.why: Decouples apps from providers; resilience and cost savings

features.name: PHI Guardrails & Content Safety
features.lookFor: Inline PHI/PII redaction, prompt-injection detection, output moderation
features.why: One enforceable HIPAA control point for AI traffic

features.name: Identity, Access & Quotas
features.lookFor: SSO, virtual keys per team, model allowlists, rate/token limits
features.why: Stops unmanaged AI use; controls PHI-eligible models

features.name: Cost Attribution & Budgets
features.lookFor: Real-time token/cost by app/team/domain, budgets, alerts, chargeback
features.why: Essential for FinOps and domain ROI

features.name: Semantic & Response Caching
features.lookFor: Exact and semantic caching, PHI-safe scoping, hit analytics
features.why: Cuts latency and cost without cross-user PHI leakage

features.name: End-to-End OTel Tracing
features.lookFor: Traces across LLM, retrieval, tool/MCP, agent hops; OTel GenAI
features.why: One view to debug agent and RAG flows

features.name: Evaluation & Quality Monitoring
features.lookFor: Automated evaluators, human feedback, drift and regression detection
features.why: Proves production quality holds; catches degradation early

features.name: Audit Logging & Retention
features.lookFor: Immutable prompt/response logs, PHI masking, retention, SIEM/Snowflake export
features.why: Supports HIPAA audit, incident response, AI regulation

features.name: Agent & MCP Traffic Governance
features.lookFor: MCP/A2A policy, tool allowlists, anomaly detection, runaway-cost protection
features.why: Governs chains of agent actions, not just calls

features.name: Deployment Portability & Overhead
features.lookFor: Self-host/BYOC, open-source core, HA, minimal added latency
features.why: In every request path; must keep PHI in-perimeter

patterns.takeaway: Best fit is Kong AI Gateway (#1, 77.5%) as the neutral, self-hosted control point for all model, MCP and A2A traffic, paired with Arize AX + Phoenix for tracing and evaluation (combined 90%), with Snowflake as the audit and analytics sink. Azure APIM + Foundry (#2, 75%) is the strongest single-suite exception path for Azure workloads, Bedrock should be consumed through Kong, LangSmith is the alternative observability choice, and Fiddler is the named PHI-guardrail add-on. Key risk is PHI redaction efficacy and unverified BAA terms for Kong and Arize, which the PoC must confirm.

platformFit.native: Cortex Agents orchestrate Cortex Analyst (semantic views) and Cortex Search over governed Gold data. Snowflake Intelligence (GA) is the business UI. RBAC, masking and row policies are inherited, Agent Identity is GA, and evaluations and OTel traces are stored in AI_OBSERVABILITY_EVENTS.
platformFit.gap: Covers data agents only: no HITL, no A2A, no PHI guardrails. Complement: one agent platform on the primary cloud (Foundry + Copilot Studio on the existing Entra/M365 estate), which calls Cortex Agents through MCP.

platformFit.native: Snowflake is not an orchestration framework. It supplies governed tools through langchain-snowflake (SnowflakeCortexAgent) and Cortex Search/Analyst as MCP tools. It can hold checkpoints, traces and TruLens evaluation results with enterprise retention policies.
platformFit.gap: Standardize on open-source LangGraph (no vendor contract), with Microsoft Agent Framework for .NET. Use LangSmith only self-hosted or under a BAA. Otherwise send OTel to the chosen observability tool.

platformFit.native: The GA Snowflake-managed MCP server exposes Cortex Agents, Analyst, Search, SQL and UDF/procedure tools under RBAC, masking, row policies and Entra/Okta OAuth. Native Apps (GA) package and distribute governed MCP servers.
platformFit.gap: No enterprise gateway or registry for non-Snowflake servers. Tools only, one spec revision behind. Complement: reuse the Pattern 6 gateway (Kong, or APIM + API Center / AgentCore Gateway) instead of adding an MCP-only vendor.

platformFit.native: AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT (OCR/LAYOUT, 2,000 pages) and AI_EXTRACT parse into Silver. SPLIT_TEXT chunking and Cortex Search hybrid retrieval with incremental TARGET_LAG refresh run on Gold. Cortex Agents combine Search with Analyst. TruLens RAG-triad evaluation is built in.
platformFit.gap: Owner's-rights permission trimming, a limited embedding catalog, and SharePoint/ECM content must be landed first. Complement: open-source LlamaIndex for complex parsing. Azure AI Search only for permission-critical SharePoint corpora.

platformFit.native: Cortex Search does managed hybrid vector + keyword + rerank (up to 400M rows per service). The native VECTOR type supports similarity functions, with Arctic/Voyage embeddings via EMBED_TEXT. Chunks and embeddings stay in Snowflake as the system of record under the BAA.
platformFit.gap: Default 20 QPS per service, no index or quantization control, minute-level lag, owner's rights. Complement: one portable Tier 1 engine (prefer Elasticsearch if already run; otherwise Qdrant), only where the PoC shows the ceilings are hit.

platformFit.native: Cortex AI Observability (TruLens traces and evaluations), Cortex AI Guardrails, AI_REDACT, Cortex usage-history views and budgets. Horizon-governed tables serve as the long-term audit, retention and chargeback sink for all AI telemetry.
platformFit.gap: No cross-platform model/MCP/A2A gateway, semantic cache or clinical PHI guardrails. Complement: Kong AI Gateway plus Arize (Phoenix OSS first), both streaming telemetry into Snowflake.

engage: One AI gateway / control plane (Kong AI Gateway, or Azure APIM + API Center if Azure-first) that also acts as the MCP/A2A gateway and private registry: one vendor covers Patterns 3 and 6.

One general-purpose agent platform matched to the primary hyperscaler (Microsoft Foundry Agent Service + Copilot Studio on the existing Entra/M365 estate), used for HITL, A2A and non-data agents, with Cortex Agents as the governed data agent behind it via MCP.
One trace/evaluation vendor under a BAA: Arize AX with Phoenix OSS first, or self-hosted LangSmith if LangGraph dominates. Pick one, not both, and export all traces to Snowflake.
Conditional: one Tier 1 vector engine (Elasticsearch if already licensed for logs/SIEM, otherwise Qdrant), only if the PoC shows Cortex Search QPS, scale or document-level trimming limits are hit.
avoid: Pinecone, Weaviate and per-pilot vector databases: Cortex Search and the native VECTOR type cover Tier 0 retrieval inside the lakehouse with no data copy and no new BAA.

Separate commercial RAG platforms, and Azure AI Search as a default index: Cortex Search + AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT/AI_EXTRACT cover governed RAG. LlamaIndex/Haystack are used as open-source libraries, not contracts.
Paid framework platforms (CrewAI Enterprise/Factory, LlamaAgents) and AutoGen/Semantic Kernel for new work: LangGraph OSS is the standard, with Microsoft Agent Framework only as the .NET path.

Stand-alone MCP gateway vendors, and Fiddler as a separate purchase: defer until the PoC shows the chosen gateway's PII sanitizer plus cloud guardrails (Bedrock Guardrails, AI_REDACT) fall short on PHI recall.
consolidation: Snowflake covers RAG natively (Strong): AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT/AI_EXTRACT feed Silver, Cortex Search indexes Gold, and Cortex Agents combine documents with claims data via Analyst. Make it the default governed retrieval path for PHI.
Make Snowflake the Tier 0 vector store and the system of record for chunks and embeddings. Any Tier 1 engine is a rebuildable derived index, which limits lock-in and vendor count.

Expose all governed data to agents only through Snowflake-managed MCP servers and Cortex Agents, so every agent platform and framework inherits RBAC, masking and row policies instead of querying data directly.

Buy one vendor per remaining gap: a single gateway that serves both model and MCP traffic, a single agent platform aligned to the primary cloud, and a single observability tool. LangGraph is open source and needs no contract.

Land all AI telemetry, costs and evaluation results in Snowflake (Snowpipe Streaming) so audit, retention and domain chargeback use existing Horizon governance and credit FinOps instead of a separate analytics tool.
